review_type: assistant visual review; not independent human annotation or ground truth
scope: Five saved final synthetic images compared with their scene descriptions and canonical synthetic references. No new generation. No automated face scores were consulted for these annotations.

rubric.people: Count visible actors separately from identity. Candidate associations are tentative role/reference matches; plausible is not a verified identity pass. Use uncertain for occlusion, small faces, ambiguous matches or possible drift.
rubric.objects: Presence concerns the required object or a recognizable candidate. Score duplicates, canonical appearance, placement, owner and state separately; a generic mug or pan does not prove the same possession.
rubric.scene_alignment: Judge broad setting and main action separately from detailed clothing, count and object-state requirements.
rubric.human_validation: Team members should independently review shuffled outputs using the same rubric before reporting majority-human results. These five scenes are a debugging pilot, not a calibrated test set.

summary.clear_count_failure: October has one visible woman and one visible man although two women and one man are requested. This does not establish which canonical female identity the cook preserves.
summary.clear_duplicate: January contains two blue mugs where one cataloged mug is requested.
summary.identity_pass_rate_reason: No independent human majority labels or calibrated identity threshold are available.

scenes.label: January - studio

people.note: Hair length, glasses and general face structure resemble the canonical portrait. Face is angled downward; this remains a tentative visual match.
Hair and beard broadly resemble the reference, but the hand and closed/downcast eyes obscure useful facial evidence.

objects.note: Olive cap with mountain motif is worn by the left character; fine wear details are not reliably resolved.
Black hardcover book is visible, but closed with a building drawing on its cover instead of open to a page sketch.
Two blue mugs sit on the desk. At least the foreground mug has a visible rim chip; duplication violates the one recurring mug intent.

scene_alignment.note: Cluttered fluorescent-lit workspace and seated tired characters are visible. Object-state and count details fail despite the broad scene match.

scenes.key_issue: Duplicate mug; sketchbook closed instead of open.

scenes.label: May - riverside drinks

people.note: Hair, glasses and face outline resemble the reference. Broad smile and side angle should not themselves count as identity drift.
Hair and beard resemble the reference; smile and profile introduce legitimate appearance variation.

objects.note: Blue bicycle with brown saddle and rear rack is beside the brick wall. Small bell, brand and wear details are not verified.
Olive cap with front patch is on the left character. The specifically requested dark grease smudge is not clearly visible.

scene_alignment.note: Riverside bench, brick wall, beer and laughter match the broad request. The specified denim jacket is absent; left character wears a short-sleeved shirt.

scenes.key_issue: Broadly successful composition; denim jacket absent; cap grease detail unclear.

scenes.label: August - birthday picnic

people.position: left foreground, glasses, seated on blanket
people.note: Glasses, straight shoulder-length hair and face outline resemble Maya. She is bareheaded; avoid using the cap alone to assign identity.

people.position: right foreground, long wavy hair, presenting cake
people.note: Long wavy hair and face/profile broadly resemble Priya, and cake-presenter role agrees with the prompt. This character wears the cap intended for Maya.
A third actor in a T-shirt is visible, but the smaller, less detailed face does not justify a confident identity judgment.

objects.note: Cap is worn by the right-hand cake presenter, tentatively Priya, while the left glasses-wearing character, tentatively Maya, is bareheaded.
Blue bicycle with brown saddle and rear rack leans near the tree; fine details are not established.
Open black book has conspicuous spiral binding, unlike the canonical hardcover bound book; it lies on the blanket, not grass. Tree-like drawing is visible.

scene_alignment.note: Sunny picnic, cake with one candle and frisbee activity are present. Character/object ownership and sketchbook construction are inconsistent.

scenes.key_issue: Cap assigned to the other foreground character; sketchbook changes to spiral binding.

scenes.label: October - kitchen

people.note: The cook fills Maya's requested role, but the face is not a confident match to the canonical portrait. Glasses, braid and apron are absent; these attribute differences alone do not establish a different identity.
Only one woman is visible although Maya and Priya are both requested. There is no separate second-woman candidate; which female identity the cook preserves is uncertain.
The seated man fills Jonah's requested role, but hair, beard and face differ noticeably from the canonical portrait. Treat as possible identity drift, not a verified mismatch.

objects.note: A small dark pan is on the stove, but it is not clearly the same canonical skillet. Yellow loose food does not clearly resemble baked cornbread.
A dark cup is on the coffee table, not the windowsill. Its color/shape do not clearly match the canonical chipped blue mug; no matching mug is visible on the sill.
Olive cap with front mountain motif hangs near the door; this broad placement requirement is met.

scene_alignment.note: Kitchen cooking and one seated person with a bowl are visible. The requested third person, large chili pot and skillet of baked cornbread are not faithfully shown.

scenes.key_issue: Only two actors; uncertain canonical identities; mug placement and skillet/cornbread mismatch.
